studies.Reference: B-Vitamin Intake from Diet and Supplements and Breast Cancer Risk in Middle-Aged Women: Results from the Prospective NutriNet-Santé Cohort.
studies.Authors: Egnell M, Fassier P, Lécuyer L, Zelek L, Vasson MP, Hercberg S, Latino-Martel P, Galan P, Deschasaux M, Touvier M
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Dietary data were collected using repeated 24 h records. A specific questionnaire assessed dietary supplement use over a 12-month period.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 27,853 women aged ≥45 years from the NutriNet-Santé cohort (2009-2016) were included
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Total thiamin intake was borderline inversely associated with breast cancer risk (HRper 1-unit increment = 0.78 (0.61, 1.00), P = 0.05)
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: borderline inversely associated with breast cancer risk

studies.Reference: Micronutrients Involved in One-Carbon Metabolism and Risk of Breast Cancer Subtypes.
studies.Authors: Cancarini I, Krogh V, Agnoli C, Grioni S, Matullo G, Pala V, Pedraglio S, Contiero P, Riva C, Muti P, Sieri S
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: B vitamin intakes were estimated from food frequency questionnaires.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 391 BCs were diagnosed among 10,786 cohort women.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: RRs were 0.61 (95% CI 0.38-0.97 highest vs. lowest quartile; P trend 0.025) for thiamine
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: protective effects of thiamine ... against BC in general

headline.funnel_interpretation: Insufficient studies to perform formal publication bias testing.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.75 (95% CI: 0.61–0.93), suggesting that Vitamin B1 is associated with a lower risk of breast cancer. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.
